quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: Drivers may not pass from either side of a ____ centerline.

options.text: Combination solid and broken yellow
Single broken yellow
Double solid yellow
Single broken white

questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no one can cross it to pass, no matter which direction they are going.

questions.question: If traffic signals at an intersection are not working due to a power outage, what should you do?

options.text: Park your vehicle off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to tell other drivers what you are doing.
Turn on hazard lights and drive through without stopping.
Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When traffic lights do not work, treat it like a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers and go through carefully when it is your turn.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Slow down when the road is wet.
The road ahead has many turns or curves.
There will be more traffic ahead.
A steep hill is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. Reduce your speed, avoid sudden stops or turns, and stay far away from the car in front of you.

questions.question: A solid white line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic goes in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic goes in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic goes in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic goes in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic goes in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic going the same way. A solid white line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: What are fluorescent pink signs used for?

options.text: Speed limit signs
Incident management signs
School zone signs
Mile markers

questions.correctAnswerText: Incident management signs
questions.explanation: Fluorescent pink signs are temporary signs that warn of problems like road closures from crashes. Pay attention when you see them.

questions.question: You come to an intersection with a flashing red light. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are coming.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, let other traffic go, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.
Take the right-of-way and go.
Drive normally.
Drive away quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and be ready to stop. Give them the right-of-way and proceed carefully to avoid hitting them.

questions.question: A steady green light at an intersection means you:

options.text: Must slow down and prepare to stop.
Must stop and check for oncoming traffic.
May go through the intersection if the road is clear.
May not turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: May go through the intersection if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can drive through the intersection if no other traffic or pedestrians are in your way. You can also turn right or left unless a sign says you cannot. Always yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: When you change lanes, you should:

options.text: Keep a safe distance from the car in front of you.
Get closer to the car in front of you.
Stop completely before changing lanes.
Quickly swerve in and out of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance from the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: Keep a safe distance when changing lanes. Check your mirrors and blind spots to make sure no cars are in the lane you want to enter.

questions.question: What colors are used for signs that show the distance to the next highway exit?

options.text: Yellow with black letters
Black with white letters
Red with white letters
Green with white letters

questions.correctAnswerText: Green with white letters
questions.explanation: Green signs with white letters give information about where you are going and how far it is.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians ahead.
End of construction zone.
School crossing ahead.
Flagger ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a person is ahead controlling traffic in a construction area.

questions.question: What do diagonal stripes sloping downward to the left on a barricade mean?

options.text: Stop.
Turn right.
Turn left.
Drive straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn left.
questions.explanation: Diagonal stripes on a barricade tell you which way to go. Stripes sloping downward to the left mean turn left. Stripes sloping downward to the right mean turn right.

questions.question: How can you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head quickly to look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder to see if your blind spot is clear. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: When traffic lights are arranged horizontally, where is the red light?

options.text: On the right.
In the middle.
On the left.
On a separate signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left.
questions.explanation: Some traffic lights are arranged horizontally. On these signals, red is on the left, yellow is in the middle, and green is on the right.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign tell you?

options.text: There is a hazard ahead or a possible danger.
You are near a school zone.
You are near a public recreation area.
Food and gas are coming up.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a hazard ahead or a possible danger.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn you about hazards or dangers. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to go the same speed as the car behind you.
Move to another lane and let the car pass.
Slow down but stay in your lane.
Let them pass and then tailgate them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane and let the car pass.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you on a multilane highway, move to the right lane to let them pass. The left lane should be used only to pass slower traffic.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad gates.
You must stop when a flagger tells you to at a railroad crossing.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Not all crossings have these devices. It is against the law to go around lowered railroad gates.

questions.question: When may you use your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you lose control of your car.
When you are passing a bicycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you lose control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to the danger.

questions.question: What shape is a stop sign?

options.text: Rectangle.
Square.
Circle.
Octagon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Octagon.
questions.explanation: Stop signs are eight-sided octagons. This shape is used only for stop signs and means you must come to a complete stop.

questions.question: How should you look to reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night?

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are too bright, look toward the right side of the road ahead. Do not look directly at the headlights because the glare can temporarily blind you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians are walking along the road ahead.
A pedestrian crossing is ahead.
Pedestrians cannot cross here.
Watch for construction workers on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: A pedestrian crossing is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a pedestrian crossing ahead. Drivers must be careful and watch for pedestrians.

questions.question: Where are stop lines (solid white lines) painted across traffic lanes?

options.text: On curves and hills.
Next to churches and schools.
At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
On freeway on-ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show where drivers must stop.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, what should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the car you passed.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use a turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane when you can see the front of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What does a defensive driver do?

options.text: Drives slowly at all times.
Watches for what other drivers do.
Drives at a constant speed.
Only drives in areas they know well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches for what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: A defensive driver watches for the actions of other drivers and expects potential problems. This helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Turn and look over your shoulder through the rear window.
Use only a backup camera.
Put your head out the driver's side window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn and look over your shoulder through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Turn your head and look through the rear window when backing up. Do not rely only on mirrors or a backup camera.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A side road is coming.
Low clearance.
Traffic is merging.
Get ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: A side road is coming.
questions.explanation: This yellow and black warning sign tells drivers to watch for traffic entering from a side road ahead.

questions.question: For a person 21 years or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent or higher.
0.08 percent or higher.
0.02 percent or higher.
0.1 percent or higher.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: Adults age 21 and older cannot drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: A curb painted ____ means a loading zone or other parking restriction.

options.text: Blue
Yellow
White
Red

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: A yellow painted curb shows a loading zone or parking restriction.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before passing and check for oncoming traffic.
Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing left.
Wait until you see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When passing, signal at least 100 feet ahead. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind spots. Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on your brakes.
Hold the steering wheel tightly and slow down gradually.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on emergency flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tightly and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not slam on the brakes. Grip the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Slow down gradually by releasing the accelerator. When you are moving slowly, apply the brakes lightly and move to a safe area off the road.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
Getting ahead of bad drivers in traffic to defend yourself.
Following the car in front of you closely.
Quickly changing lanes to move through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you spot dangerous situations and take action before an accident happens. It helps you avoid crashes with reckless, careless, or drunk drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Move to the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Let emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens pass first, no matter which direction they are going. Move to the right side of the road and stop right away. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then move to the right and stop.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: It is summer.
You must stop and back up immediately.
Driving conditions are not ideal.
You should drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and show that work is being done on or near the road. Be very careful when you see these signs.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When you are driving through an intersection.
When you are passing a cyclist.
When you see a child about to run into the street.
When you are parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who do not see you. For example, honk if a child starts to run into the street in front of your car.

questions.question: When driving down a long or steep hill, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors for fast traffic behind you.
Assume all traffic is going the same speed.
Look over your shoulder for traffic behind you.
Press the brake pedal hard to control other cars' speeds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for fast traffic behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when driving downhill because vehicles often speed up. Watch out for large trucks and buses that may be going too fast.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic goes in opposite directions and you cannot pass.
Traffic goes in opposite directions and you can pass when safe.
Traffic goes in the same direction and you cannot pass.
Traffic goes in the same direction and you can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic goes in opposite directions and you cannot pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. Solid lines mean you cannot pass.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a curve or hill because it is unlikely another car is coming.
By driving on the shoulder of the road.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or curves because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never drive onto the shoulder to pass. Do not pass over a solid yellow line.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle in a small car, be prepared for:

options.text: Loud noises.
Extra air pollution.
Strong wind from the large vehicle.
Vehicle parts falling off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller cars. Be ready to steer correctly when passing or approaching large vehicles moving at high speeds.

questions.question: You have the right-of-way when turning left on which traffic light?

options.text: A solid green light
A flashing yellow light
A green arrow pointing left
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A green arrow pointing left
questions.explanation: A solid green arrow means you can drive in the direction the arrow points. Oncoming traffic must stop.

questions.question: Which describes a defensive driver?

options.text: Anticipation
Passivity
Easily distracted
Anger

questions.correctAnswerText: Anticipation
questions.explanation: Defensive drivers keep a safe distance from other cars. They expect problems and take action to avoid them.
